loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Fresh validation is preferred; policy may require it for high-risk semantic gates.

next_loop.reason: The next compiler loop should start from CodeWiki source refs; the agent may refresh context when useful.

requirements.text: Implement forward promotion gates and backward ambiguity routes before lower-priority remediation work proceeds.
Provide machine-readable inline approval surfaces for decisions and task candidates.
Automate routine compiler/gateway progression through bounded agency while preserving hard gates and context reset safety.
Make parallel sprint/task work safe with scheduler partitioning, artifact claims, worktrees/refs, fresh validation, and publisher proof.
Define production-ready quality gates with deterministic checks, review thresholds/waivers, content proof, and validation evidence.

assumptions: The existing remediation roadmap remains useful but should not be the next implementation focus until foundational pipeline work is validated.
The UI approval surface can initially target Pi TUI/compact panel with explicit non-interactive fallback.
Parallel scheduler may initially support local worktrees/refs and plan-only external orchestration before full worker spawning.
non_goals: Do not implement source changes in the planning loop.
Do not delete existing PyLens remediation tasks.
Do not bypass the decision build/gateway that created this plan.
risks: SPRINT-009 is high risk because it changes CodeWiki's own workflow gates; implementation should use narrow artifact claims and fresh validation.
Parallel scheduler/publisher queue work may need additional decision rows if implementation reveals Git/publication semantics not covered by this decision.
Quality profile thresholds must avoid blocking all existing work without waiver escape hatches.
